Gospel Journey 3D actors — sources and adaptations

Current production revision: gospel-modern-2026-10-26.
Run modernize-actors.py for the current YoungJesus, AdultJesus and Mary models.
It finishes with continuous garment seams, corrected youth cuff coverage,
loose linen shaping and a rounded youth lower face. All three models export the
same GospelRig transform paths and seven CC0 animation takes. Cloth, hair and
face geometry are intentionally redesigned; the earlier mesh-preservation
report describes the previous remaster only. Prior models and reports remain
in History/before-modern-2026-10-26. Modern renders and the current FBX reimport
report provide separate current evidence.

body-soft-albedo.png is a generated colour refinement of the licensed original
UV atlas. The original atlas remains unchanged; source/generation hashes are
recorded in soft-skin-generation.json. No third-party game texture is used.

Base character anatomy, eyes, eyebrows and hairstyle meshes:
Quaternius — Universal Base Characters, Standard FREE edition.
https://quaternius.com/packs/universalbasecharacters.html
https://quaternius.itch.io/universal-base-characters
License: CC0 1.0 Universal. Original notice: Source/License_Standard.txt.

Skeletal motion:
Quaternius — Universal Animation Library, Standard FREE edition.
https://quaternius.com/packs/universalanimationlibrary.html
https://quaternius.itch.io/universal-animation-library
License: CC0 1.0 Universal. Original notice: Source/Animation-License.txt.
Selected source takes: Idle_Loop, Walk_Loop, Jog_Fwd_Loop,
Jump_Start, Jump_Loop, Jump_Land, Interact.
Interact is presented as a nonviolent reaching/hand movement in the optional
practice area. It is not an attack against a story character or a Bible event.

This project adapts the game-ready base to clothed youth/adult story characters:
linen tunic, woven cuffs/belt, sandals, adult mantle, youth proportions,
material tinting and compatible rig retargeting. These are artistic depictions,
not a historical reconstruction of Jesus' physical appearance. The body is a
continuous skinned mesh with modeled eyes/hands/feet, not primitive proxy parts.
Only the selected CC0 Standard files are used; no paid/source/pro editions.

Tools/Art/Gospel3D/build-actors.py reproduces the adaptation and FBX export.
Tools/Art/Gospel3D/augment-actions.py adds the four action takes to the preserved
production actors and combines matching-material skinned parts. It retains all
65 bones, modeled vertices/triangles, skinning, and the named Eyes renderer.
Tools/Art/Gospel3D/verify-actions.py reimports all three exported FBXs and samples
all seven takes. Its report covers Blender assets, not Unity gameplay.
Resources/Art/Gospel3D/material-spec.json defines the URP material inputs.
Generated Blender review images are art previews, not Unity gameplay evidence.
Unity animation, contact and runtime rendering require separate validation.
